name: Myth on Trial
why_it_works: Everyone carries a few beliefs they never checked. Naming one out loud creates a small itch (am I wrong?), and watching it get tested on screen scratches it. The brand that corrects you gently becomes the brand you trust.

hook.pattern: State the myth as if it is true, stamp it ON TRIAL, and let the viewer wonder which side wins.

variables.name: myth
variables.description: The common belief, written the way customers say it, starting with a capital letter, 6 words or fewer

variables.name: why_people_believe
variables.description: The honest reason the myth sounds right, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: Scrubbing cleans pots, so it feels right for teeth

variables.name: evidence
variables.description: A simple, showable test or fact that settles it, 12 words or fewer
variables.example: Hard scrubbing wears gum lines back and leaves plaque in the grooves

variables.name: truth
variables.description: The corrected rule in one short line, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: Soft bristles, small circles, two full minutes

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer can do next, starting with a verb, 6 words or fewer

beats.purpose: hook: state the myth and put it on trial

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a wooden courtroom gavel resting beside an everyday object tied to the myth '{{myth}}', dramatic single overhead spotlight, dark background, room at top for bold text

beats.purpose: the case for the myth, said fairly

visual.prompt: Vertical candid photo of an ordinary person doing the habit behind '{{myth}}' at home, natural window light, mid shot, slightly worried expression
Vertical 9:16 macro close-up demonstrating '{{evidence}}', clean studio light, slow push-in, shallow depth of field, clinical but warm color
Client-supplied photo of a real {{brand}} team member demonstrating the right way, '{{truth}}', bright clean workspace, eye-level mid shot

cta: Comment the next myth to test. {{offer}}.

craft.notes: Argue the myth's side honestly for one beat before you knock it down. Viewers who believed it feel understood, not stupid, so they keep watching to the verdict instead of getting defensive and scrolling.

do_not: Mock people who believed the myth; the viewer is one of them
Pick a myth so obscure nobody has heard it, or so obvious nobody believes it
Pile on three myths; one myth per reel, save the rest for a series
compliance: Dental and chiropractic: general education only, add 'Not medical advice, ask your provider' on screen; no diagnosis or cure claims
Any health claim in the evidence beat must be backed by a published source you can cite in the caption
Skincare: cosmetic claims only (look, feel); never say a product treats, heals or cures a condition
Fitness: no guaranteed body or weight results; add 'Consult a professional before starting a new exercise' on any form or training myth
